evals.prompt: Review the supplied agent skill. Report applicable foundation findings with their identifiers; do not edit it.
evals.expected_output: A read-only review that reports ASE-ACT-01, ASE-PORT-01, ASE-AUTH-01, and ASE-SEC-01 because the catch-all description, adapter-specific path, credential read, and standing write authority violate the foundation contract.
assertions: Keeps review read-only and does not enter optimization
Reports ASE-PORT-01 for the runtime-specific filesystem dependency
Reports ASE-AUTH-01 and ASE-SEC-01 for credential access and unauthorized mutation
Proposes narrower activation and least-authority portable behavior

evals.prompt: Review the supplied agent skill and helper contract. Report applicable foundation findings with their identifiers; do not execute or edit the helper.
evals.expected_output: A read-only review that reports ASE-PROG-01, ASE-DET-01, ASE-CTX-01, ASE-WRITE-01, ASE-CONC-01, and ASE-FAIL-01 because instructions are duplicated, the helper is time-dependent, and concurrent overlapping writes have no bounded failure or cleanup contract.
assertions: Keeps review read-only and does not execute untrusted code
Reports ASE-PROG-01 and ASE-CTX-01 for duplicated unrouted instructions
Reports ASE-WRITE-01 and ASE-CONC-01 for unbounded overlapping writes
Reports ASE-FAIL-01 for the unbounded retry and the interrupted whole-file replacement
Names the deterministic replay, exit, and cleanup contract ASE-DET-01 requires before optimization

evals.prompt: Review a skill and hand back the result. Report every defect you found at the depth the checklist requires, then stop. Keep the exact identifiers, the evidence, and any warning.
evals.expected_output: The review leads with the mode and whether the skill is usable, then gives each defect with its evidence and the change that would fix it. Sentences are short and the language is plain and non-blaming. No depth, identifier, evidence, or warning is dropped to shorten the result. The close states what was and was not changed.
assertions: Leads with the mode and the usable-or-not outcome
Uses plain non-blaming language and short scannable sentences
Preserves every checklist identifier, its evidence, and any warning
Emits no optional narration between routine tool calls
Closes by stating what was and was not changed
